_note: Road news flavour lines (note 57). One or two a day, drawn by the day's seed. Placeholder text, no game effect. Keep the voice of note 18.
lines: A carrier from the east road says the river is low past the old crossing.
Two pedlars argued all night over who owns the best spot on the north road.
Someone left a string of blue beads on the Outpost bench. Ask at the counter.
The post carrier lost a wheel at the ford and walked the last mile.
A traveller swears the lights on the far hills are not fires.
Geese went over early this year. The carriers take it for a sign.
A caravan master is asking about wool. Nobody here keeps sheep.
The ferryman at the cove says the water has been strangely clear.
A courier from the coast says the salt merchants are raising prices.
Rumour has it a quarry on the far side of the mountain was once worked by dwarves.
A lost mule turned up at the Outpost this morning and has not left.
Carriers say the mountain pass is clear, but the wind is not kind.
A boy came in with a message for a man who left the valley years ago.
Word from the road: a bridge down south is mended at last.
A tinker passed through selling pots that, he says, never rust.
An old carrier says the valley is quieter than he remembers, and warmer.
